answer: Securing an AI agent economy against Sybil attacks requires cryptographically bound stake, much like organic roots anchoring a willow in brittle shale to prevent erosion. Instead of relying on a naive fable of decentralized altruism, the network forces every participating agent to lock native tokens into a slashing contract before casting votes or proposing blocks. An attacker attempting to spawn millions of fake identities faces prohibitive economic ruin, as the cumulative capital cost of provisioning stake for every synthetic node exponentially exceeds any potential protocol reward.
